solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sick of being rained on?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: standing beneath the rain clouds

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as fed up with getting wet; the idiom for feeling poorly also describes, word for word, someone standing out in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mildly ill, and taken literally it places a person beneath falling rain.

clue.text: Ill-equipped force brigade encircles

indicators.note: to encircle is to surround, so the brigade word wraps around the force letter

parts.note: a brigade is a military unit
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A poorly supplied fire brigade or army brigade surrounds some enemy force.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unsuitable or lacking the right kit for a task is not fit for it.

clue.text: Seriously, pork pies and Tango can be most toxic

parts.note: informal intensifier: dead good means seriously good
rhyming slang: pork pies means lies
T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A warning that pork pies washed down with Tango, a British fizzy orange drink, are seriously bad for you.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pies is Cockney rhyming slang (often shortened to porkies) for lies; Tango is also a British soft drink, which helps the food-and-drink surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deadliest kills most surely, so it is the most poisonous or harmful of its kind.

clue.text: Check about bar closing earlier than usual

indicators.note: a pub shutting early loses its final hour, so the bar word loses its final letter

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
an inn is a pub, a bar

explanation.surface: Someone queries a pub that calls last orders early.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or hold back, as a rider controls a horse with the reins.

clue.text: Painter painting in pig and horse

indicators.note: in places the painting word inside the animal words that follow

parts.note: a hog is a pig
painting is a form of art
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: An artist whose canvas shows a pig and a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth was an 18th-century English painter and satirist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogarth was a celebrated English painter and engraver, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Hopeful embargo will be lifted in fall

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the word for fall

parts.note: to wane is to fall or decline

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting a word turns it upwards, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an embargo is a ban on trade

explanation.surface: An optimist hopes a trade embargo will be lifted in the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall looks like the American word for autumn, but it means decline here.
explanation.definitionFit: A wannabe is an aspiring person, a hopeful who wants to become someone famous.

clue.text: Lock tackled by expert southern players

indicators.note: being tackled means being held by, so the lock word is gripped by the expert word

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a lock of hair is a tress
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A rugby lock forward is brought down by skilled players from a southern team.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a lock is a forward position, which the surface plays on; here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Actresses are female performers in plays, so players in the theatrical sense.

clue.text: Some pious types get into this addiction

definitions.text: Some pious types get into this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the robe worn by monks and nuns

explanation.surface: Some devout people get hooked on a vice.
explanation.walkthrough: Get into reads as becoming involved in a habit, but it is putting on a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a monk's or nun's long garment and a hard-to-break dependency.

clue.text: Bearded tits led singer astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters stray out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some birds lured a singer off the right path.
explanation.walkthrough: The bearded tit, also called the bearded reedling, is a small reedbed bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedling is another name for the bearded tit, a small bird of reedbeds.

clue.text: Fiery bird Ovid originally dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so that letter is removed from the bird

parts.note: a flamingo is a pink wading bird

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the opening letter of Ovid is used

parts.note: the first letter of Ovid

explanation.surface: The Roman poet Ovid waved away a fiery bird like the phoenix.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaming describes something burning with flames, hence blazing and fiery.

clue.text: Totally incompetent celebrity

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split as two words
second meaning: a famous or prominent person

explanation.surface: A sneering verdict on a useless famous person.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words the answer reads not able, which is totally incompetent.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a person of distinction or fame, which is what a celebrity is.

clue.text: Porky dog needs to be picked up

indicators.note: picked up suggests caught by the ear, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: A fat dog that needs lifting up.
explanation.walkthrough: Porky looks like an adjective for the dog, but it is the noun: porky is British rhyming slang (from pork pie) for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A porky is a lie, and a tale is a made-up story or falsehood, as in telling tales.

clue.text: Over time, no real man dances for show

indicators.note: dancing moves things about, so the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Given enough time, a fake man ends up dancing just to put on a display.
explanation.walkthrough: Over time here means with time on top, adding the time letter to the fodder before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornamental is decorative rather than useful, there purely to be looked at.

clue.text: One spotted adulterer in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: an adulterer cheats on a spouse

explanation.surface: An unfaithful partner was seen out talking with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in a non-rhotic British accent, where the final r of cheater is not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a big cat with a spotted coat, so it is literally one that is spotted.

clue.text: Egalitarian conservative girl? Not so much!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a lass is a girl
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Asking whether a traditional young woman really believes in equality, then answering that she hardly does.
explanation.definitionFit: A classless society has no social hierarchy, so everyone is treated as equal.

clue.text: Fun follows after Queen punches brown bear

indicators.note: following after means coming behind, so the fun word sits at the end
a fist that punches goes into something, so the Queen letter goes inside the colour word

parts.note: tan is a light brown
R for Regina, Latin for queen
sport can mean fun or amusement

explanation.surface: A queen punches a brown bear, and fun is had afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown bear looks like one animal, but brown is the colour and bear is the verb meaning carry.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to carry it, and to transport is likewise to carry from place to place.

clue.text: Character in record store close to Bonn

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a silo stores grain

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of Bonn

explanation.surface: A figure seen in a record shop near the German city of Bonn.
explanation.walkthrough: Character looks like a person in the shop, but it is a letter of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a written character.

clue.text: A huge ball thrown for comic

indicators.note: something thrown is tossed around, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedian has an enormous ball lobbed at him.
explanation.walkthrough: Comic reads as a noun, a comedian, but the definition is the adjective meaning funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comic is funny enough to make people laugh, so it is risible or ridiculous.

clue.text: Draw a model-type that's a bundle of nerves

parts.note: taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous early car
in anatomy a tract is a bundle of nerve fibres

explanation.surface: Sketch a nervous fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: A bundle of nerves sounds like an anxious person; here it is the anatomical term.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to pull it in, which is what attracting people means.

clue.text: Hit Republican leader hard around lunchtime?

indicators.note: around puts the leader word on either side of the lunchtime letter

parts.note: Donald Trump leads the US Republican Party
lunch is often at one o'clock, and I is the Roman numeral one
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A political leader is struck hard around the middle of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose leap from lunchtime to one o'clock and then to the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit is a great success, and a triumph is likewise a notable victory or success.

clue.text: Treat flying saucer with bit of scepticism

parts.note: an athletics discus is a saucer-shaped disc thrown through the air

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter of it, here the opening one

parts.note: the first letter of scepticism

explanation.surface: Regard reports of a UFO with some doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: Flying saucer suggests a UFO, but it describes the disc thrown in athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a subject is to deal with it in speech or writing, which is to discuss it.

clue.text: Belittle one's lawyer during row

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so these pieces sit inside the row word

parts.note: a din is a loud row or noise
one's read as one is: I for one, then the S of the contraction
a DA is a US district attorney

explanation.surface: Someone runs down their own lawyer in the middle of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: One's gives I (one) plus S; DA is the American district attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: To disdain someone is to look down on them with scorn, which belittles them.

clue.text: Most ostentatious criminal steals ship

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The flashiest crook of all makes off with a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Splashy means showy and attention-grabbing, so the superlative is the most showy of all.

clue.text: One likely to bait lake and two rivers

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An angler readies bait beside a lake where two rivers meet.
explanation.walkthrough: Two rivers gives one named river, the Ure in Yorkshire, plus the standard abbreviation R.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurer entices or tempts others into a trap, just as baiting does.

clue.text: Country fellow swaps daughter for piano!

indicators.note: to swap one thing for another is to replace it, so one letter is exchanged

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
D is the abbreviation for daughter
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A rural man gives up his daughter in exchange for a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Country fellow reads as a rustic, but country is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked country in north-central Africa.

clue.text: Get into gear and drive East with sons

parts.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for drive
E is the abbreviation for east
S is the abbreviation for son, twice for sons

explanation.surface: Start the car and head east with the boys.
explanation.walkthrough: Get into gear and drive sounds like motoring, but gear is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is informal for clothes, so getting into gear means putting clothes on.

clue.text: American takes out nobles, not Tory leader

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: toffs are upper-class people, the nobility

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of Tory is used

parts.note: the first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: An American assassin eliminates aristocrats, sparing the Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In American slang to off someone is to kill them; toff is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: Offs is US slang for kills, so it matches takes out in the violent sense, written for an American speaker.

clue.text: Unforgettable air of war Rome aroused

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A haunting tune about ancient Rome stirred up for war.
explanation.definitionFit: An earworm is a catchy tune that sticks in the head, a melody you cannot forget.

clue.text: Good-natured female taken in by a story

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it

parts.note: a fable is a story
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A kindly woman falls for a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An affable person is friendly and easy to talk to, which is to be good-natured.

clue.text: Longer chess test arranged as exercise

indicators.note: arranging puts things in a chosen order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lengthy chess exam is set up as a training drill.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means going for a short walk, especially after sitting, which is light exercise.
